types.name: DiagramObject
types.summary: An object that defines one or more points in a given space. This object can be associated with anything that specializes IdentifiedObject. For single line diagrams such objects typically include such items as analog values, breakers, disconnectors, power transformers, and transmission lines.

fields.name: Diagram
fields.summary: A diagram object is part of a diagram.

fields.name: DiagramObjectPoints
fields.summary: A diagram object can have 0 or more points to reflect its layout position, routing (for polylines) or boundary (for polygons).

fields.name: DiagramObjectStyle
fields.summary: A diagram object has a style associated that provides a reference for the style used in the originating system.

fields.name: VisibilityLayers
fields.summary: A diagram object can be part of multiple visibility layers.

fields.name: drawingOrder
fields.summary: The drawing order of this element. The higher the number, the later the element is drawn in sequence. This is used to ensure that elements that overlap are rendered in the correct order.

fields.name: isPolygon
fields.summary: Defines whether or not the diagram objects points define the boundaries of a polygon or the routing of a polyline. If this value is true then a receiving application should consider the first and last points to be connected.

fields.name: offsetX
fields.summary: The offset in the X direction. This is used for defining the offset from centre for rendering an icon (the default is that a single point specifies the centre of the icon). The offset is in per-unit with 0 indicating there is no offset from the horizontal centre of the icon. -0.5 indicates it is offset by 50% to the left and 0.5 indicates an offset of 50% to the right.

fields.name: offsetY
fields.summary: The offset in the Y direction. This is used for defining the offset from centre for rendering an icon (the default is that a single point specifies the centre of the icon). The offset is in per-unit with 0 indicating there is no offset from the vertical centre of the icon. The offset direction is dependent on the orientation of the diagram, with -0.5 and 0.5 indicating an offset of +/- 50% on the vertical axis.

fields.name: rotation
fields.summary: Sets the angle of rotation of the diagram object. Zero degrees is pointing to the top of the diagram. Rotation is clockwise. DiagramObject.rotation=0 has the following meaning: The connection point of an element which has one terminal is pointing to the top side of the diagram. The connection point "From side" of an element which has more than one terminal is pointing to the top side of the diagram. DiagramObject.rotation=90 has the following meaning: The connection point of an element which has one terminal is pointing to the right hand side of the diagram. The connection point "From side" of an element which has more than one terminal is pointing to the right hand side of the diagram.

types.name: UnitMultiplier
types.summary: The unit multipliers defined for the CIM. When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single- character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type. For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "�" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "k�". For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g". If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram. As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "�", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "m�", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

enumValues.name: none
enumValues.summary: No multiplier or equivalently multiply by 1.

types.name: UnitSymbol
types.summary: The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole. Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single- letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol. To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3 or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "�" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol. Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units. The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

enumValues.name: lineOpen
enumValues.summary: The fault is when the conductor path is broken between two terminals. Additional coexisting faults may be required if the broken conductor also causes connections to grounds or other lines or phases.

enumValues.name: lineToGround
enumValues.summary: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground. The line to line fault impedance is not used and assumed infinite. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground, but not between the phases.

enumValues.name: lineToLine
enumValues.summary: The fault connects the specified phases together without a connection to ground. The ground impedance of this fault is ignored. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault. A single phase fault should not be specified.

enumValues.name: lineToLineToGround
enumValues.summary: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground and to each other. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault in a full mesh. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault. A single phase fault should not be specified. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground.

fields.summary: Fraction of power from shaft 2 intermediate pressure turbine output.

fields.name: shaft2PowerLP1
fields.summary: Fraction of power from shaft 2 first low pressure turbine output.

fields.name: shaft2PowerLP2
fields.summary: Fraction of power from shaft 2 second low pressure turbine output.

fields.name: steamChestTC
fields.summary: Steam chest time constant.

types.name: Subcritical
types.summary: Once-through subcritical boiler.

types.name: Supercritical
types.summary: Once-through supercritical boiler.

types.name: AirCompressor
types.summary: Combustion turbine air compressor which is an integral part of a compressed air energy storage (CAES) plant.

fields.name: airCompressorRating
fields.summary: Rating of the CAES air compressor.

types.name: BatteryStateKind
types.summary: The state of the battery unit.

enumValues.name: empty
enumValues.summary: Unable to discharge, and not charging.

enumValues.name: full
enumValues.summary: Unable to charge, and not discharging.

enumValues.name: waiting
enumValues.summary: Neither charging nor discharging, but able to do so.

types.name: BatteryUnit
types.summary: An electrochemical energy storage device.

fields.name: batteryState
fields.summary: The current state of the battery (charging, full, etc.).

fields.name: ratedE
fields.summary: Full energy storage capacity of the battery. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: storedE
fields.summary: Amount of energy currently stored. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero and lower than BatteryUnit.ratedE.

types.name: CAESPlant
types.summary: Compressed air energy storage plant.

fields.name: AirCompressor
fields.summary: An air compressor may be a member of a compressed air energy storage plant.

fields.name: ThermalGeneratingUnit
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may be a member of a compressed air energy storage plant.

fields.name: energyStorageCapacity
fields.summary: The rated energy storage capacity. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: ratedCapacityP
fields.summary: The CAES plant's gross rated generating capacity. The attribute shall be a positive value.

types.name: CogenerationPlant
types.summary: A set of thermal generating units for the production of electrical energy and process steam (usually from the output of the steam turbines). The steam sendout is typically used for industrial purposes or for municipal heating and cooling.

fields.name: SteamSendoutSchedule
fields.summary: A cogeneration plant has a steam sendout schedule.

fields.name: ThermalGeneratingUnits
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may be a member of a cogeneration plant.

fields.name: cogenHPSendoutRating
fields.summary: The high pressure steam sendout.

fields.name: cogenHPSteamRating
fields.summary: The high pressure steam rating.

fields.name: cogenLPSendoutRating
fields.summary: The low pressure steam sendout.

fields.name: cogenLPSteamRating
fields.summary: The low pressure steam rating.

fields.name: ratedP
fields.summary: The rated output active power of the cogeneration plant. The attribute shall be a positive value.

types.name: CombinedCyclePlant
types.summary: A set of combustion turbines and steam turbines where the exhaust heat from the combustion turbines is recovered to make steam for the steam turbines, resulting in greater overall plant efficiency.

fields.name: ThermalGeneratingUnits
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may be a member of a combined cycle plant.

fields.name: combCyclePlantRating
fields.summary: The combined cycle plant's active power output rating.

types.name: EmissionAccount
types.summary: Accounts for tracking emissions usage and credits for thermal generating units. A unit may have zero or more emission accounts, and will typically have one for tracking usage and one for tracking credits.

fields.name: emissionType
fields.summary: The type of emission, for example sulfur dioxide (SO2). The y1AxisUnits of the curve contains the unit of measure (e.g. kg) and the emissionType is the type of emission (e.g. sulfur dioxide).

fields.name: emissionValueSource
fields.summary: The source of the emission value.

types.name: EmissionCurve
types.summary: Relationship between the unit's emission rate in units of mass per hour (Y- axis) and output active power (X-axis) for a given type of emission. This curve applies when only one type of fuel is being burned.

fields.name: emissionContent
fields.summary: The emission content per quantity of fuel burned.

fields.name: emissionType
fields.summary: The type of emission, which also gives the production rate measurement unit. The y1AxisUnits of the curve contains the unit of measure (e.g. kg) and the emissionType is the type of emission (e.g. sulfur dioxide).

fields.name: isNetGrossP
fields.summary: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

types.name: EmissionType
types.summary: The type of emission.

types.name: EmissionValueSource
types.summary: The source of the emission value.

types.name: FossilFuel
types.summary: The fossil fuel consumed by the non-nuclear thermal generating unit. For example, coal, oil, gas, etc. These are the specific fuels that the generating unit can consume.

fields.name: FuelAllocationSchedules
fields.summary: A fuel allocation schedule shall have a fossil fuel.

fields.name: ThermalGeneratingUnit
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have one or more fossil fuels.

fields.name: fossilFuelType
fields.summary: The type of fossil fuel, such as coal, oil, or gas.

fields.name: fuelCost
fields.summary: The cost in terms of heat value for the given type of fuel.

fields.name: fuelDispatchCost
fields.summary: The cost of fuel used for economic dispatching which includes: fuel cost, transportation cost, and incremental maintenance cost.

fields.name: fuelEffFactor
fields.summary: The efficiency factor for the fuel (per unit) in terms of the effective energy absorbed.

fields.name: fuelHandlingCost
fields.summary: Handling and processing cost associated with this fuel.

fields.name: fuelHeatContent
fields.summary: The amount of heat per weight (or volume) of the given type of fuel.

fields.name: fuelMixture
fields.summary: Relative amount of the given type of fuel, when multiple fuels are being consumed.

fields.name: fuelSulfur
fields.summary: The fuel's fraction of pollution credit per unit of heat content.

fields.name: highBreakpointP
fields.summary: The active power output level of the unit at which the given type of fuel is switched on. This fuel (e.g., oil) is sometimes used to supplement the base fuel (e.g., coal) at high active power output levels.

fields.name: lowBreakpointP
fields.summary: The active power output level of the unit at which the given type of fuel is switched off. This fuel (e.g., oil) is sometimes used to stabilize the base fuel (e.g., coal) at low active power output levels.

types.name: FuelAllocationSchedule
types.summary: The amount of fuel of a given type which is allocated for consumption over a specified period of time.

fields.name: fuelAllocationEndDate
fields.summary: The end time and date of the fuel allocation schedule.

fields.name: fuelAllocationStartDate
fields.summary: The start time and date of the fuel allocation schedule.

fields.name: fuelType
fields.summary: The type of fuel, which also indicates the corresponding measurement unit.

fields.name: maxFuelAllocation
fields.summary: The maximum amount of fuel that is allocated for consumption for the scheduled time period.

fields.name: minFuelAllocation
fields.summary: The minimum amount of fuel that is allocated for consumption for the scheduled time period, e.g., based on a "take-or-pay" contract.

types.name: FuelType
types.summary: Type of fuel.

enumValues.name: coal
enumValues.summary: Generic coal, not including lignite type.

enumValues.name: lignite
enumValues.summary: The fuel is lignite coal. Note that this is a special type of coal, so the other enum of coal is reserved for hard coal types or if the exact type of coal is not known.

enumValues.name: other
enumValues.summary: Any fuel type not included in the rest of the enumerated value.

types.name: GenUnitOpCostCurve
types.summary: Relationship between unit operating cost (Y-axis) and unit output active power (X-axis). The operating cost curve for thermal units is derived from heat input and fuel costs. The operating cost curve for hydro units is derived from water flow rates and equivalent water costs.

fields.name: isNetGrossP
fields.summary: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

types.name: GenUnitOpSchedule
types.summary: The generating unit's Operator-approved current operating schedule (or plan), typically produced with the aid of unit commitment type analyses. The X-axis represents absolute time. The Y1-axis represents the status (0=off-line and unavailable: 1=available: 2=must run: 3=must run at fixed power value: etc.). The Y2-axis represents the must run fixed power value where required.

types.name: GeneratingUnit
types.summary: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

fields.name: GenUnitOpCostCurves
fields.summary: A generating unit may have one or more cost curves, depending upon fuel mixture and fuel cost.

fields.name: GenUnitOpSchedule
fields.summary: A generating unit may have an operating schedule, indicating the planned operation of the unit.

fields.name: GrossToNetActivePowerCurves
fields.summary: A generating unit may have a gross active power to net active power curve, describing the losses and auxiliary power requirements of the unit.

fields.name: RotatingMachine
fields.summary: A synchronous machine may operate as a generator and as such becomes a member of a generating unit.

fields.name: allocSpinResP
fields.summary: The planned unused capacity (spinning reserve) which can be used to support emergency load.

fields.name: autoCntrlMarginP
fields.summary: The planned unused capacity which can be used to support automatic control overruns.

fields.name: baseP
fields.summary: For dispatchable units, this value represents the economic active power basepoint, for units that are not dispatchable, this value represents the fixed generation value. The value shall be between the operating low and high limits.

fields.name: controlDeadband
fields.summary: Unit control error deadband. When a unit's desired active power change is less than this deadband, then no control pulses will be sent to the unit.

fields.name: controlPulseHigh
fields.summary: Pulse high limit which is the largest control pulse that the unit can respond to.

fields.name: controlPulseLow
fields.summary: Pulse low limit which is the smallest control pulse that the unit can respond to.

fields.name: controlResponseRate
fields.summary: Unit response rate which specifies the active power change for a control pulse of one second in the most responsive loading level of the unit.

fields.name: efficiency
fields.summary: The efficiency of the unit in converting mechanical energy, from the prime mover, into electrical energy.

fields.name: genControlMode
fields.summary: The unit control mode.

fields.name: genControlSource
fields.summary: The source of controls for a generating unit. Defines the control status of the generating unit.

fields.name: governorMPL
fields.summary: Governor motor position limit.

fields.name: governorSCD
fields.summary: Governor Speed Changer Droop. This is the change in generator power output divided by the change in frequency normalized by the nominal power of the generator and the nominal frequency and expressed in percent and negated. A positive value of speed change droop provides additional generator output upon a drop in frequency.

fields.name: highControlLimit
fields.summary: High limit for secondary (AGC) control.

fields.name: initialP
fields.summary: Default initial active power which is used to store a powerflow result for the initial active power for this unit in this network configuration.

fields.name: longPF
fields.summary: Generating unit long term economic participation factor.

fields.name: lowControlLimit
fields.summary: Low limit for secondary (AGC) control.

fields.name: lowerRampRate
fields.summary: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be lowered by control actions.

fields.name: maxEconomicP
fields.summary: Maximum high economic active power limit, that should not exceed the maximum operating active power limit.

fields.name: maxOperatingP
fields.summary: This is the maximum operating active power limit the dispatcher can enter for this unit.

fields.name: maximumAllowableSpinningReserve
fields.summary: Maximum allowable spinning reserve. Spinning reserve will never be considered greater than this value regardless of the current operating point.

fields.name: minEconomicP
fields.summary: Low economic active power limit that shall be greater than or equal to the minimum operating active power limit.

fields.name: minOperatingP
fields.summary: This is the minimum operating active power limit the dispatcher can enter for this unit.

fields.name: minimumOffTime
fields.summary: Minimum time interval between unit shutdown and startup.

fields.name: modelDetail
fields.summary: Detail level of the generator model data.

fields.name: nominalP
fields.summary: The nominal power of the generating unit. Used to give precise meaning to percentage based attributes such as the governor speed change droop (governorSCD attribute). The attribute shall be a positive value equal to or less than RotatingMachine. ratedS.

fields.name: normalPF
fields.summary: Generating unit economic participation factor. The sum of the participation factors across generating units does not have to sum to one. It is used for representing distributed slack participation factor. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

fields.name: penaltyFactor
fields.summary: Defined as: 1 / ( 1 - Incremental Transmission Loss); with the Incremental Transmission Loss expressed as a plus or minus value. The typical range of penalty factors is (0.9 to 1.1).

fields.name: raiseRampRate
fields.summary: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be raised by control actions.

fields.name: ratedGrossMaxP
fields.summary: The unit's gross rated maximum capacity (book value). The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: ratedGrossMinP
fields.summary: The gross rated minimum generation level which the unit can safely operate at while delivering power to the transmission grid. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: ratedNetMaxP
fields.summary: The net rated maximum capacity determined by subtracting the auxiliary power used to operate the internal plant machinery from the rated gross maximum capacity. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: shortPF
fields.summary: Generating unit short term economic participation factor.

fields.name: startupCost
fields.summary: The initial startup cost incurred for each start of the GeneratingUnit.

fields.name: startupTime
fields.summary: Time it takes to get the unit on-line, from the time that the prime mover mechanical power is applied.

fields.name: tieLinePF
fields.summary: Generating unit economic participation factor.

fields.name: totalEfficiency
fields.summary: The efficiency of the unit in converting the fuel into electrical energy.

fields.name: variableCost
fields.summary: The variable cost component of production per unit of ActivePower.

types.name: GeneratorControlMode
types.summary: Unit control modes.

types.name: GeneratorControlSource
types.summary: The source of controls for a generating unit.

types.name: GrossToNetActivePowerCurve
types.summary: Relationship between the generating unit's gross active power output on the X- axis (measured at the terminals of the machine(s)) and the generating unit's net active power output on the Y-axis (based on utility-defined measurements at the power station). Station service loads, when modelled, should be treated as non-conforming bus loads. There may be more than one curve, depending on the auxiliary equipment that is in service.

types.name: HeatInputCurve
types.summary: Relationship between unit heat input in energy per time for main fuel (Y1-axis) and supplemental fuel (Y2-axis) versus unit output in active power (X-axis). The quantity of main fuel used to sustain generation at this output level is prorated for throttling between definition points. The quantity of supplemental fuel used at this output level is fixed and not prorated.

fields.name: auxPowerMult
fields.summary: Power output - auxiliary power multiplier adjustment factor.

fields.name: auxPowerOffset
fields.summary: Power output - auxiliary power offset adjustment factor.

fields.name: heatInputEff
fields.summary: Heat input - efficiency multiplier adjustment factor.

fields.name: heatInputOffset
fields.summary: Heat input - offset adjustment factor.

fields.name: isNetGrossP
fields.summary: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

types.name: HeatRateCurve
types.summary: Relationship between unit heat rate per active power (Y-axis) and unit output (X-axis). The heat input is from all fuels.

fields.name: isNetGrossP
fields.summary: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

types.name: HydroEnergyConversionKind
types.summary: Specifies the capability of the hydro generating unit to convert energy as a generator or pump.

enumValues.name: generator
enumValues.summary: Able to generate power, but not able to pump water for energy storage.

enumValues.name: pumpAndGenerator
enumValues.summary: Able to both generate power and pump water for energy storage.

types.name: HydroGeneratingEfficiencyCurve
types.summary: Relationship between unit efficiency as percentage and unit output active power for a given net head in meters. The relationship between efficiency, discharge, head, and power output is expressed as follows: E =KP/HQ where: E is the efficiency, as a percentage; P is the active power; H is the height; Q is the discharge, volume/time unit; K is a constant. For example, a curve instance for a given net head could show efficiency (Y- axis) versus active power output (X-axis) or versus discharge on the X-axis.

types.name: HydroGeneratingUnit
types.summary: A generating unit whose prime mover is a hydraulic turbine (e.g., Francis, Pelton, Kaplan).

fields.name: HydroGeneratingEfficiencyCurves
fields.summary: A hydro generating unit has an efficiency curve.

fields.name: PenstockLossCurve
fields.summary: A hydro generating unit has a penstock loss curve.

fields.name: TailbayLossCurve
fields.summary: A hydro generating unit has a tailbay loss curve.

fields.name: dropHeight
fields.summary: The height water drops from the reservoir mid-point to the turbine.

fields.name: energyConversionCapability
fields.summary: Energy conversion capability for generating.

fields.name: hydroUnitWaterCost
fields.summary: The equivalent cost of water that drives the hydro turbine.

fields.name: turbineType
fields.summary: Type of turbine.

types.name: HydroPlantStorageKind
types.summary: The type of hydro power plant.

types.name: HydroPowerPlant
types.summary: A hydro power station which can generate or pump. When generating, the generator turbines receive water from an upper reservoir. When pumping, the pumps receive their water from a lower reservoir.

fields.name: GenSourcePumpDischargeReservoir
fields.summary: Generators are supplied water from or pumps discharge water to an upstream reservoir.

fields.name: HydroGeneratingUnits
fields.summary: The hydro generating unit belongs to a hydro power plant.

fields.name: HydroPumps
fields.summary: The hydro pump may be a member of a pumped storage plant or a pump for distributing water.

fields.name: Reservoir
fields.summary: Generators discharge water to or pumps are supplied water from a downstream reservoir.

fields.name: dischargeTravelDelay
fields.summary: Water travel delay from tailbay to next downstream hydro power station.

fields.name: genRatedP
fields.summary: The hydro plant's generating rating active power for rated head conditions. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: hydroPlantStorageType
fields.summary: The type of hydro power plant water storage.

fields.name: penstockType
fields.summary: Type and configuration of hydro plant penstock(s).

fields.name: plantDischargeCapacity
fields.summary: Total plant discharge capacity.

fields.name: plantRatedHead
fields.summary: The plant's rated gross head. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: pumpRatedP
fields.summary: The hydro plant's pumping rating active power for rated head conditions. The attribute shall be a positive value.

fields.name: surgeTankCode
fields.summary: A code describing the type (or absence) of surge tank that is associated with the hydro power plant.

fields.name: surgeTankCrestLevel
fields.summary: The level at which the surge tank spills.

types.name: HydroPump
types.summary: A synchronous motor-driven pump, typically associated with a pumped storage plant.

fields.name: HydroPumpOpSchedule
fields.summary: The hydro pump has a pumping schedule over time, indicating when pumping is to occur.

fields.name: pumpDischAtMaxHead
fields.summary: The pumping discharge under maximum head conditions, usually at full gate.

fields.name: pumpDischAtMinHead
fields.summary: The pumping discharge under minimum head conditions, usually at full gate.

fields.name: pumpPowerAtMaxHead
fields.summary: The pumping power under maximum head conditions, usually at full gate.

fields.name: pumpPowerAtMinHead
fields.summary: The pumping power under minimum head conditions, usually at full gate.

types.name: HydroPumpOpSchedule
types.summary: The hydro pump's Operator-approved current operating schedule (or plan), typically produced with the aid of unit commitment type analyses. The unit's operating schedule status is typically given as: (0=unavailable) (1=available to startup or shutdown) (2=must pump).

types.name: IncrementalHeatRateCurve
types.summary: Relationship between unit incremental heat rate in (delta energy/time) per (delta active power) and unit output in active power. The IHR curve represents the slope of the HeatInputCurve. Note that the "incremental heat rate" and the "heat rate" have the same engineering units.

fields.name: isNetGrossP
fields.summary: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

types.name: InflowForecast
types.summary: Natural water inflow to a reservoir, usually forecasted from predicted rain and snowmelt. Typically in one hour increments for up to 10 days. The forecast is given in average cubic meters per second over the time increment.

types.name: LevelVsVolumeCurve
types.summary: Relationship between reservoir volume and reservoir level. The volume is at the Y-axis and the reservoir level at the X-axis.

types.name: NuclearGeneratingUnit
types.summary: A nuclear generating unit.

types.name: PenstockLossCurve
types.summary: Relationship between penstock head loss (in meters) and total discharge through the penstock (in cubic meters per second). One or more turbines may be connected to the same penstock.

types.name: PhotoVoltaicUnit
types.summary: A photovoltaic device or an aggregation of such devices.

types.name: PowerElectronicsUnit
types.summary: A generating unit or battery or aggregation that connects to the AC network using power electronics rather than rotating machines.

fields.name: maxP
fields.summary: Maximum active power limit. This is the maximum (nameplate) limit for the unit.

fields.name: minP
fields.summary: Minimum active power limit. This is the minimum (nameplate) limit for the unit.

types.name: PowerElectronicsWindUnit
types.summary: A wind generating unit that connects to the AC network with power electronics rather than rotating machines or an aggregation of such units.

types.name: Reservoir
types.summary: A water storage facility within a hydro system, including: ponds, lakes, lagoons, and rivers. The storage is usually behind some type of dam.

fields.name: InflowForecasts
fields.summary: A reservoir may have a "natural" inflow forecast.

fields.name: LevelVsVolumeCurves
fields.summary: A reservoir may have a level versus volume relationship.

fields.name: SpillsIntoReservoirs
fields.summary: A reservoir may spill into a downstream reservoir.

fields.name: TargetLevelSchedule
fields.summary: A reservoir may have a water level target schedule.

fields.name: activeStorageCapacity
fields.summary: Storage volume between the full supply level and the normal minimum operating level.

fields.name: energyStorageRating
fields.summary: The reservoir's energy storage rating in energy for given head conditions.

fields.name: fullSupplyLevel
fields.summary: Full supply level, above which water will spill. This can be the spillway crest level or the top of closed gates.

fields.name: grossCapacity
fields.summary: Total capacity of reservoir.

fields.name: normalMinOperateLevel
fields.summary: Normal minimum operating level below which the penstocks will draw air.

fields.name: riverOutletWorks
fields.summary: River outlet works for riparian right releases or other purposes.

fields.name: spillTravelDelay
fields.summary: The spillway water travel delay to the next downstream reservoir.

fields.name: spillWayGateType
fields.summary: Type of spillway gate, including parameters.

fields.name: spillwayCapacity
fields.summary: The flow capacity of the spillway in cubic meters per second.

fields.name: spillwayCrestLength
fields.summary: The length of the spillway crest.

fields.name: spillwayCrestLevel
fields.summary: Spillway crest level above which water will spill.

types.name: ShutdownCurve
types.summary: Relationship between the rate in gross active power/minute (Y-axis) at which a unit should be shutdown and its present gross MW output (X-axis).

fields.name: shutdownCost
fields.summary: Fixed shutdown cost.

fields.name: shutdownDate
fields.summary: The date and time of the most recent generating unit shutdown.

types.name: SolarGeneratingUnit
types.summary: A solar thermal generating unit, connected to the grid by means of a rotating machine. This class does not represent photovoltaic (PV) generation.

types.name: StartIgnFuelCurve
types.summary: The quantity of ignition fuel (Y-axis) used to restart and repay the auxiliary power consumed versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

fields.name: ignitionFuelType
fields.summary: Type of ignition fuel.

types.name: StartMainFuelCurve
types.summary: The quantity of main fuel (Y-axis) used to restart and repay the auxiliary power consumed versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

fields.name: mainFuelType
fields.summary: Type of main fuel.

types.name: StartRampCurve
types.summary: Rate in gross active power per minute (Y-axis) at which a unit can be loaded versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

fields.name: hotStandbyRamp
fields.summary: The startup ramp rate in gross for a unit that is on hot standby.

types.name: StartupModel
types.summary: Unit start up characteristics depending on how long the unit has been off line.

fields.name: StartIgnFuelCurve
fields.summary: The unit's startup model may have a startup ignition fuel curve.

fields.name: StartMainFuelCurve
fields.summary: The unit's startup model may have a startup main fuel curve.

fields.name: StartRampCurve
fields.summary: The unit's startup model may have a startup ramp curve.

fields.name: fixedMaintCost
fields.summary: Fixed maintenance cost.

fields.name: hotStandbyHeat
fields.summary: The amount of heat input per time unit required for hot standby operation.

fields.name: incrementalMaintCost
fields.summary: Incremental maintenance cost.

fields.name: minimumDownTime
fields.summary: The minimum number of hours the unit must be down before restart.

fields.name: minimumRunTime
fields.summary: The minimum number of hours the unit must be operating before being allowed to shut down.

fields.name: riskFactorCost
fields.summary: The opportunity cost associated with the return in monetary unit. This represents the restart's "share" of the unit depreciation and risk of an event which would damage the unit.

fields.name: startupCost
fields.summary: Total miscellaneous start up costs.

fields.name: startupDate
fields.summary: The date and time of the most recent generating unit startup.

fields.name: startupPriority
fields.summary: Startup priority within control area where lower numbers indicate higher priorities. More than one unit in an area may be assigned the same priority.

fields.name: stbyAuxP
fields.summary: The unit's auxiliary active power consumption to maintain standby mode.

types.name: SteamSendoutSchedule
types.summary: The cogeneration plant's steam sendout schedule in volume per time unit.

types.name: TailbayLossCurve
types.summary: Relationship between tailbay head loss height (Y-axis) and the total discharge into the power station's tailbay volume per time unit (X-axis) . There could be more than one curve depending on the level of the tailbay reservoir or river level.

types.name: TargetLevelSchedule
types.summary: Reservoir water level targets from advanced studies or "rule curves". Typically in one hour increments for up to 10 days.

fields.name: highLevelLimit
fields.summary: High target level limit, above which the reservoir operation will be penalized.

fields.name: lowLevelLimit
fields.summary: Low target level limit, below which the reservoir operation will be penalized.

types.name: ThermalGeneratingUnit
types.summary: A generating unit whose prime mover could be a steam turbine, combustion turbine, or diesel engine.

fields.name: EmissionCurves
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have one or more emission curves.

fields.name: EmmissionAccounts
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have one or more emission allowance accounts.

fields.name: FuelAllocationSchedules
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have one or more fuel allocation schedules.

fields.name: HeatInputCurve
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have a heat input curve.

fields.name: HeatRateCurve
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have a heat rate curve.

fields.name: IncrementalHeatRateCurve
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have an incremental heat rate curve.

fields.name: ShutdownCurve
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have a shutdown curve.

fields.name: StartupModel
fields.summary: A thermal generating unit may have a startup model.

fields.name: oMCost
fields.summary: Operating and maintenance cost for the thermal unit.

types.name: WindGenUnitKind
types.summary: Kind of wind generating unit.

enumValues.name: offshore
enumValues.summary: The wind generating unit is located offshore.

enumValues.name: onshore
enumValues.summary: The wind generating unit is located onshore.

types.name: WindGeneratingUnit
types.summary: A wind driven generating unit, connected to the grid by means of a rotating machine. May be used to represent a single turbine or an aggregation.

fields.name: windGenUnitType
fields.summary: The kind of wind generating unit.

types.name: ApplicationSecurityKind
types.summary: Specifies the expected security mechanism, per IEC 62351-4, to be utilized.

enumValues.name: endToEndSecure
enumValues.summary: Indicates that E2E-security shall be used in order to allow establishment of an MMS association.

enumValues.name: nonSecure
enumValues.summary: Indicates that an application security shall not be used in order to allow establishment of an MSS association.

enumValues.name: secure
enumValues.summary: Indicates that the A-security-profile as specified in Clause 11 (or IEC TS 62351-4:2007) shall be used in order to allow establishment of an MMS association.

types.name: BilateralExchangeActor
types.summary: BilateralExchangeActor describes an actor that provides ICCP data, consumes ICCP data or both. The ICCP data provider lists the data it makes available to an ICCP data consumer. This data is described by ProvidedBilateralPoints. The relation between an ICCP data provider and a consumer is established by a BilateralExchangeAgreement. types.name: LoadResponseCharacteristic
types.summary: Models the characteristic response of the load demand due to changes in system conditions such as voltage and frequency. It is not related to demand response. If LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is True, the exponential voltage or frequency dependent models are specified and used as to calculate active and reactive power components of the load model. The equations to calculate active and reactive power components of the load model are internal to the power flow calculation, hence they use different quantities depending on the use case of the data exchange. The equations for exponential voltage dependent load model injected power are: pInjection= Pnominal* (Voltage/cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage) ** cim: LoadResponseCharacteristic.pVoltageExponent qInjection= Qnominal* (Voltage/cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage) ** cim: LoadResponseCharacteristic.qVoltageExponent Where: 1) * means "multiply" and ** is "raised to power of"; 2) Pnominal and Qnominal represent the active power and reactive power at nominal voltage as any load described by the voltage exponential model shall be given at nominal voltage. This means that EnergyConsumer.p and EnergyConsumer. q are at nominal voltage. 3) After power flow is solved: -pInjection and qInjection correspond to SvPowerflow.p and SvPowerflow.q respectively. - Voltage corresponds to SvVoltage.v at the TopologicalNode where the load is connected.

fields.name: exponentModel
fields.summary: Indicates the exponential voltage dependency model is to be used. If false, the coefficient model is to be used. The exponential voltage dependency model consist of the attributes: - pVoltageExponent - qVoltageExponent - pFrequencyExponent - qFrequencyExponent. The coefficient model consist of the attributes: - pConstantImpedance - pConstantCurrent - pConstantPower - qConstantImpedance - qConstantCurrent - qConstantPower. The sum of pConstantImpedance, pConstantCurrent and pConstantPower shall equal 1. The sum of qConstantImpedance, qConstantCurrent and qConstantPower shall equal 1.

types.name: Measurement
types.summary: A Measurement represents any measured, calculated or non-measured non- calculated quantity. Any piece of equipment may contain Measurements, e.g. a substation may have temperature measurements and door open indications, a transformer may have oil temperature and tank pressure measurements, a bay may contain a number of power flow measurements and a Breaker may contain a switch status measurement. The PSR - Measurement association is intended to capture this use of Measurement and is included in the naming hierarchy based on EquipmentContainer. The naming hierarchy typically has Measurements as leaves, e.g. Substation- VoltageLevel-Bay-Switch-Measurement. Some Measurements represent quantities related to a particular sensor location in the network, e.g. a voltage transformer (VT) or potential transformer (PT) at a busbar or a current transformer (CT) at the bar between a breaker and an isolator. The sensing position is not captured in the PSR - Measurement association. Instead it is captured by the Measurement - Terminal association that is used to define the sensing location in the network topology. The location is defined by the connection of the Terminal to ConductingEquipment. If both a Terminal and PSR are associated, and the PSR is of type ConductingEquipment, the associated Terminal should belong to that ConductingEquipment instance. When the sensor location is needed both Measurement-PSR and Measurement- Terminal are used. The Measurement-Terminal association is never used alone.

The phase information in Measurement, along with 'measurementType' and 'phases' uniquely defines a Measurement for a device, based on normal network phase. Their meaning will not change when the computed energizing phasing is changed due to jumpers or other reasons. If the attribute is missing three phases (ABC) shall be assumed.

fields.name: operatorBlocked

fields.name: oscillatory
fields.summary: To prevent some overload of the communication it is sensible to detect and suppress oscillating (fast changing) binary inputs. If a signal changes in a defined time twice in the same direction (from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0) then oscillation is detected and the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" is set. If it is detected a configured numbers of transient changes could be passed by. In this time the validity status "questionable" is set. If after this defined numbers of changes the signal is still in the oscillating state the value shall be set either to the opposite state of the previous stable value or to a defined default value. In this case the validity status "questionable" is reset and "invalid" is set as long as the signal is oscillating. If it is configured such that no transient changes should be passed by then the validity status "invalid" is set immediately in addition to the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" (used for status information only).

fields.name: outOfRange
fields.summary: Measurement value is beyond a predefined range of value.

fields.name: overFlow
fields.summary: Measurement value is beyond the capability of being represented properly. For example, a counter value overflows from maximum count back to a value of zero.

fields.name: source
fields.summary: Source gives information related to the origin of a value. The value may be acquired from the process, defaulted or substituted.

fields.name: suspect
fields.summary: A correlation function has detected that the value is not consistent with other values. Typically set by a network State Estimator.

fields.name: test
fields.summary: Measurement value is transmitted for test purposes.

fields.name: validity
fields.summary: Validity of the measurement value.
