fields.name: normalValue
fields.summary: Normal value for Control.value e.g. used for percentage scaling.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: The value representing the actuator output.

types.name: StringMeasurement
types.summary: StringMeasurement represents a measurement with values of type string.

types.name: StringMeasurementValue
types.summary: StringMeasurementValue represents a measurement value of type string.

fields.name: StringMeasurement
fields.summary: Measurement to which this value is connected.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: The value to supervise.

types.name: Validity
types.summary: Validity for MeasurementValue.

enumValues.name: GOOD
enumValues.summary: The value is marked good if no abnormal condition of the acquisition function or the information source is detected.

enumValues.name: INVALID
enumValues.summary: The value is marked invalid when a supervision function recognises abnormal conditions of the acquisition function or the information source (missing or non-operating updating devices). The value is not defined under this condition. The mark invalid is used to indicate to the client that the value may be incorrect and shall not be used.

enumValues.name: QUESTIONABLE
enumValues.summary: The value is marked questionable if a supervision function detects an abnormal behaviour, however the value could still be valid. The client is responsible for determining whether or not values marked "questionable" should be used.

types.name: ValueAliasSet
types.summary: Describes the translation of a set of values into a name and is intendend to facilitate custom translations. Each ValueAliasSet has a name, description etc. A specific Measurement may represent a discrete state like Open, Closed, Intermediate etc. This requires a translation from the MeasurementValue.value number to a string, e.g. 0->"Invalid", 1->"Open", 2->"Closed", 3- >"Intermediate". Each ValueToAlias member in ValueAliasSet.Value describe a mapping for one particular value to a name.

fields.name: Discretes
fields.summary: The Measurements using the set for translation.

fields.name: Values
fields.summary: The ValueToAlias mappings included in the set.

types.name: ValueToAlias
types.summary: Describes the translation of one particular value into a name, e.g. 1 as "Open".

fields.name: value
fields.summary: The value that is mapped.

types.name: ActivePowerLimit
types.summary: Limit on active power flow.

fields.name: normalValue
fields.summary: The normal value of active power limit. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: Value of active power limit. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

types.name: ApparentPowerLimit
types.summary: Apparent power limit.

fields.name: normalValue
fields.summary: The normal apparent power limit. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: The apparent power limit. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

types.name: BranchGroup
types.summary: A group of branch terminals whose directed flow summation is to be monitored. A branch group need not form a cutset of the network.

fields.name: BranchGroupTerminal
fields.summary: The directed branch group terminals to be summed.

fields.name: maximumActivePower
fields.summary: The maximum active power flow.

fields.name: maximumReactivePower
fields.summary: The maximum reactive power flow.

fields.name: minimumActivePower
fields.summary: The minimum active power flow.

fields.name: minimumReactivePower
fields.summary: The minimum reactive power flow.

fields.name: monitorActivePower
fields.summary: Monitor the active power flow.

fields.name: monitorReactivePower
fields.summary: Monitor the reactive power flow.

types.name: BranchGroupTerminal
types.summary: A specific directed terminal flow for a branch group.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.summary: The terminal to be summed.

fields.name: positiveFlowIn
fields.summary: The flow into the terminal is summed if set true. The flow out of the terminal is summed if set false.

types.name: CurrentLimit
types.summary: Operational limit on current.

fields.name: normalValue
fields.summary: The normal value for limit on current flow. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: Limit on current flow. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

types.name: OperationalLimit
types.summary: A value and normal value associated with a specific kind of limit. The sub class value and normalValue attributes vary inversely to the associated OperationalLimitType.acceptableDuration (acceptableDuration for short). If a particular piece of equipment has multiple operational limits of the same kind (apparent power, current, etc.), the limit with the greatest acceptableDuration shall have the smallest limit value and the limit with the smallest acceptableDuration shall have the largest limit value. Note: A large current can only be allowed to flow through a piece of equipment for a short duration without causing damage, but a lesser current can be allowed to flow for a longer duration.

fields.name: LimitDependencyModel
fields.summary: The limit dependency models which are used to calculate this limit. If no limit dependencies are specified then the native limit value is used.

fields.name: OperationalLimitType
fields.summary: The limit type associated with this limit.

types.name: OperationalLimitDirectionKind
types.summary: The direction attribute describes the side of a limit that is a violation.

enumValues.name: absoluteValue
enumValues.summary: An absoluteValue limit means that a monitored absolute value above the limit value is a violation.

enumValues.name: high
enumValues.summary: High means that a monitored value above the limit value is a violation. If applied to a terminal flow, the positive direction is into the terminal.

enumValues.name: low
enumValues.summary: Low means a monitored value below the limit is a violation. If applied to a terminal flow, the positive direction is into the terminal.

types.name: OperationalLimitSet
types.summary: A set of limits associated with equipment. Sets of limits might apply to a specific temperature, or season for example. A set of limits may contain different severities of limit levels that would apply to the same equipment. The set may contain limits of different types such as apparent power and current limits or high and low voltage limits that are logically applied together as a set.

fields.name: Equipment
fields.summary: The equipment to which the limit set applies.

fields.name: OperationalLimitValue
fields.summary: Values of equipment limits.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.summary: The terminal where the operational limit set apply.

types.name: OperationalLimitType
types.summary: The operational meaning of a category of limits.

fields.name: acceptableDuration
fields.summary: The nominal acceptable duration of the limit. Limits are commonly expressed in terms of the time limit for which the limit is normally acceptable. The actual acceptable duration of a specific limit may depend on other local factors such as temperature or wind speed. The attribute has meaning only if the flag isInfiniteDuration is set to false, hence it shall not be exchanged when isInfiniteDuration is set to true.

fields.name: direction
fields.summary: The direction of the limit.

fields.name: isInfiniteDuration
fields.summary: Defines if the operational limit type has infinite duration. If true, the limit has infinite duration. If false, the limit has definite duration which is defined by the attribute acceptableDuration.

types.name: VoltageLimit
types.summary: Operational limit applied to voltage. The use of operational VoltageLimit is preferred instead of limits defined at VoltageLevel. The operational VoltageLimits are used, if present.

fields.name: normalValue
fields.summary: The normal limit on voltage. High or low limit nature of the limit depends upon the properties of the operational limit type. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

fields.name: value
fields.summary: Limit on voltage. High or low limit nature of the limit depends upon the properties of the operational limit type. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

types.name: CurrentRelay
types.summary: A device that checks current flow values in any direction or designated direction.

fields.name: currentLimit1
fields.summary: Current limit number one 1 for inverse time pickup.

fields.name: currentLimit2
fields.summary: Current limit number 2 for inverse time pickup.

fields.name: currentLimit3
fields.summary: Current limit number 3 for inverse time pickup.

fields.name: inverseTimeFlag
fields.summary: Set true if the current relay has inverse time characteristic.

fields.name: timeDelay1
fields.summary: Inverse time delay number 1 for current limit number 1.

fields.name: timeDelay2
fields.summary: Inverse time delay number 2 for current limit number 2.

fields.name: timeDelay3
fields.summary: Inverse time delay number 3 for current limit number 3.

types.name: ProtectionEquipment
types.summary: An electrical device designed to respond to input conditions in a prescribed manner and after specified conditions are met to cause contact operation or similar abrupt change in associated electric control circuits, or simply to display the detected condition. Protection equipment is associated with conducting equipment and usually operate circuit breakers.

fields.name: ConductingEquipments
fields.summary: Protection equipment may be used to protect specific conducting equipment.

fields.name: ProtectedSwitches
fields.summary: Protected switches operated by this ProtectionEquipment.

fields.name: ProtectiveAction
fields.summary: Protective action can emulate the action done by one or more protection equipment. In a node breaker model were protective equipment is model this association will be used.

fields.name: highLimit
fields.summary: The maximum allowable value.

fields.name: lowLimit
fields.summary: The minimum allowable value.

fields.name: powerDirectionFlag
fields.summary: Direction same as positive active power flow value.

fields.name: relayDelayTime
fields.summary: The time delay from detection of abnormal conditions to relay operation.

fields.name: unitMultiplier
fields.summary: The unit multiplier of the value.

fields.name: unitSymbol
fields.summary: The unit of measure of the value.

types.name: RecloseSequence
types.summary: A reclose sequence (open and close) is defined for each possible reclosure of a breaker.

fields.name: recloseDelay
fields.summary: Indicates the time lapse before the reclose step will execute a reclose.

fields.name: recloseStep
fields.summary: Indicates the ordinal position of the reclose step relative to other steps in the sequence.

types.name: SynchrocheckRelay
types.summary: A device that operates when two AC circuits are within the desired limits of frequency, phase angle, and voltage, to permit or to cause the paralleling of these two circuits. Used to prevent the paralleling of non-synchronous topological islands.

fields.name: maxAngleDiff
fields.summary: The maximum allowable voltage vector phase angle difference across the open device.

fields.name: maxFreqDiff
fields.summary: The maximum allowable frequency difference across the open device.

fields.name: maxVoltDiff
fields.summary: The maximum allowable difference voltage across the open device.

types.name: CommunicationLink
types.summary: The connection to remote units is through one or more communication links. Reduntant links may exist. The CommunicationLink class inherits PowerSystemResource. The intention is to allow CommunicationLinks to have Measurements. These Measurements can be used to model link status as operational, out of service, unit failure etc.

fields.name: BilateralExchangeActor
fields.summary: ICCP data provider or consumer using communication addressing for a Bilateral table.

fields.name: RemoteUnits
fields.summary: RTUs may be attached to communication links.

types.name: RemoteControl
types.summary: Remote controls are outputs that are sent by the remote unit to actuators in the process.

fields.name: Control
fields.summary: The Control for the RemoteControl point.

fields.name: actuatorMaximum
fields.summary: The maximum set point value accepted by the remote control point.

fields.name: actuatorMinimum
fields.summary: The minimum set point value accepted by the remote control point.

fields.name: remoteControlled
fields.summary: Set to true if the actuator is remotely controlled.

types.name: RemotePoint
types.summary: For an RTU, remote points correspond to telemetered values or control outputs. Other units (e.g. control centres) usually also contain calculated values.

types.name: RemoteSource
types.summary: Remote sources are state variables that are telemetered or calculated within the remote unit.

fields.name: deadband
fields.summary: The smallest change in value to be reported.

fields.name: scanInterval
fields.summary: The time interval between scans.

fields.name: sensorMaximum
fields.summary: The maximum value the telemetry item can return.

fields.name: sensorMinimum
fields.summary: The minimum value the telemetry item can return.

types.name: RemoteUnit
types.summary: A remote unit can be an RTU, IED, substation control system, control centre, etc. The communication with the remote unit can be through various standard protocols (e.g. IEC 61870, IEC 61850) or non standard protocols (e.g. DNP, RP570, etc.). A remote unit contains remote data points that might be telemetered, collected or calculated. The RemoteUnit class inherits PowerSystemResource. The intention is to allow RemoteUnits to have Measurements. These Measurements can be used to model unit status as operational, out of service, unit failure, etc.

fields.name: RemotePoints
fields.summary: Remote points this Remote unit contains.

fields.name: remoteUnitType
fields.summary: Type of remote unit.

types.name: RemoteUnitType
types.summary: Type of remote unit.

types.name: Source
types.summary: Source gives information related to the origin of a value.

enumValues.name: DEFAULTED
enumValues.summary: The value contains a default value.

enumValues.name: PROCESS
enumValues.summary: The value is provided by input from the process I/O or being calculated from some function.

enumValues.name: SUBSTITUTED
enumValues.summary: The value is provided by input of an operator or by an automatic source.

types.name: StateVariable
types.summary: An abstract class for state variables.

types.name: SvInjection
types.summary: The SvInjection reports the calculated bus injection minus the sum of the terminal flows. The terminal flow is positive out from the bus (load sign convention) and bus injection has positive flow into the bus. SvInjection may have the remainder after state estimation or slack after power flow calculation.

fields.name: TopologicalNode
fields.summary: The topological node associated with the flow injection state variable.

fields.name: pInjection
fields.summary: The active power mismatch between calculated injection and initial injection. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus).

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The terminal phase at which the connection is applied. If missing, the injection is assumed to be balanced among non-neutral phases.

fields.name: qInjection
fields.summary: The reactive power mismatch between calculated injection and initial injection. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus).

types.name: SvPowerFlow
types.summary: State variable for power flow. Load convention is used for flow direction. This means flow out from the TopologicalNode into the equipment is positive.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.summary: The terminal associated with the power flow state variable.

fields.name: m_EnergyGroup
fields.summary: The energygroup

fields.name: p
fields.summary: The active power flow. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The individual phase of the flow. If unspecified, then assumed to be balanced among phases.

fields.name: q
fields.summary: The reactive power flow. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

types.name: SvShuntCompensatorSections
types.summary: State variable for the number of sections in service for a shunt compensator.

fields.name: ShuntCompensator
fields.summary: The shunt compensator for which the state applies.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The terminal phase at which the connection is applied. If missing, the injection is assumed to be balanced among non-neutral phases.

fields.name: sections
fields.summary: The number of sections in service as a continuous variable. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero. To get integer value scale with ShuntCompensator. bPerSection.

types.name: SvStatus
types.summary: State variable for status.

fields.name: ConductingEquipment
fields.summary: The conducting equipment associated with the status state variable.

fields.name: inService
fields.summary: The in service status as a result of topology processing. It indicates if the equipment is considered as energized by the power flow. It reflects if the equipment is connected within a solvable island. It does not necessarily reflect whether or not the island was solved by the power flow.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The individual phase status. If the attribute is unspecified, then three phase model is assumed.

types.name: SvSwitch
types.summary: State variable for switch.

fields.name: Switch
fields.summary: The switch associated with the switch state.

fields.name: open
fields.summary: The attribute tells if the computed state of the switch is considered open.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The terminal phase at which the connection is applied. If missing, the injection is assumed to be balanced among non-neutral phases.

types.name: SvTapStep
types.summary: State variable for transformer tap step.

fields.name: TapChanger
fields.summary: The tap changer associated with the tap step state.

fields.name: position
fields.summary: The floating point tap position. This is not the tap ratio, but rather the tap step position as defined by the related tap changer model and normally is constrained to be within the range of minimum and maximum tap positions.

types.name: SvVoltage
types.summary: State variable for voltage.

fields.name: TopologicalNode
fields.summary: The topological node associated with the voltage state.

fields.name: angle
fields.summary: The voltage angle of the topological node complex voltage with respect to system reference.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: If specified the voltage is the line to ground voltage of the individual phase. If unspecified, then the voltage is assumed balanced.

fields.name: v
fields.summary: The voltage magnitude at the topological node. The attribute shall be a positive value.

types.name: BusNameMarker
types.summary: Used to apply user standard names to TopologicalNodes. Associated with one or more terminals that are normally connected with the bus name. The associated terminals are normally connected by non-retained switches. For a ring bus station configuration, all BusbarSection terminals in the ring are typically associated. For a breaker and a half scheme, both BusbarSections would normally be associated. For a ring bus, all BusbarSections would normally be associated. For a "straight" busbar configuration, normally only the main terminal at the BusbarSection would be associated.

fields.name: ReportingGroup
fields.summary: The reporting group to which this bus name marker belongs.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.summary: The terminals associated with this bus name marker.

fields.name: TopologicalNode
fields.summary: A user defined topological node that was originally defined in a planning model not yet having topology described by ConnectivityNodes. Once ConnectivityNodes has been created they may linked to user defined ToplogicalNdes using BusNameMarkers.

fields.name: priority
fields.summary: Priority of bus name marker for use as topology bus name. Use 0 for do not care. Use 1 for highest priority. Use 2 as priority is less than 1 and so on.

types.name: TopologicalIsland
types.summary: An electrically connected subset of the network. Topological islands can change as the current network state changes, e.g. due to: - disconnect switches or breakers changing state in a SCADA/EMS. - manual creation, change or deletion of topological nodes in a planning tool. Only energised TopologicalNode-s shall be part of the topological island.

fields.name: AngleRefTopologicalNode
fields.summary: The angle reference for the island. Normally there is one TopologicalNode that is selected as the angle reference for each island. Other reference schemes exist, so the association is typically optional.

fields.name: TopologicalNodes
fields.summary: A topological node belongs to a topological island.

types.name: TopologicalNode
types.summary: For a detailed substation model a topological node is a set of connectivity nodes that, in the current network state, are connected together through any type of closed switches, including jumpers. Topological nodes change as the current network state changes (i.e., switches, breakers, etc. change state). For a planning model, switch statuses are not used to form topological nodes. Instead they are manually created or deleted in a model builder tool. Topological nodes maintained this way are also called "busses".

fields.name: BaseVoltage
fields.summary: The base voltage of the topological node.

fields.name: ConnectivityNodeContainer
fields.summary: The connectivity node container to which the topological node belongs.

fields.name: ConnectivityNodes
fields.summary: The connectivity nodes combine together to form this topological node. May depend on the current state of switches in the network.

fields.name: ReportingGroup
fields.summary: The reporting group to which the topological node belongs.

fields.name: Terminal
fields.summary: The terminals associated with the topological node. This can be used as an alternative to the connectivity node path to terminal, thus making it unnecessary to model connectivity nodes in some cases. Note that if connectivity nodes are in the model, this association would probably not be used as an input specification.

fields.name: pInjection
fields.summary: The active power injected into the bus at this location in addition to injections from equipment. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus). Starting value for a steady state solution.

fields.name: qInjection
fields.summary: The reactive power injected into the bus at this location in addition to injections from equipment. Positive sign means injection into the TopologicalNode (bus). Starting value for a steady state solution.

types.name: ACLineSegment
types.summary: A wire or combination of wires, with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry alternating current between points in the power system. For symmetrical, transposed three phase lines, it is sufficient to use attributes of the line segment, which describe impedances and admittances for the entire length of the segment. Additionally impedances can be computed by using length and associated per length impedances. The BaseVoltage at the two ends of ACLineSegments in a Line shall have the same BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage. However, boundary lines may have slightly different BaseVoltage.nominalVoltages and variation is allowed. Larger voltage difference in general requires use of an equivalent branch.

fields.name: Clamp
fields.summary: The clamps connected to the line segment.

fields.name: WireSpacingInfo
fields.summary: The wire spacing information that applies to this AC line segment

fields.name: b0ch
fields.summary: Zero sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

fields.name: bch
fields.summary: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section. This value represents the full charging over the full length of the line.

fields.name: g0ch
fields.summary: Zero sequence shunt (charging) conductance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

fields.name: gch
fields.summary: Positive sequence shunt (charging) conductance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

fields.name: r
fields.summary: Positive sequence series resistance of the entire line section.

fields.name: r0
fields.summary: Zero sequence series resistance of the entire line section.

fields.name: shortCircuitEndTemperature
fields.summary: Maximum permitted temperature at the end of SC for the calculation of minimum short-circuit currents. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: x
fields.summary: Positive sequence series reactance of the entire line section.

fields.name: x0
fields.summary: Zero sequence series reactance of the entire line section.

types.name: ACLineSegmentPhase
types.summary: Represents a single wire of an alternating current line segment.

fields.name: ACLineSegment
fields.summary: The line segment to which the phase belongs.

fields.name: WireInfo
fields.summary: Wire information contributing to this AC line segment phase information.

fields.name: phase
fields.summary: The phase connection of the wire at both ends.

fields.name: sequenceNumber
fields.summary: Number designation for this line segment phase. Each line segment phase within a line segment should have a unique sequence number. This is useful for unbalanced modelling to bind the mathematical model (PhaseImpedanceData of PerLengthPhaseImpedance) with the connectivity model (this class) and the physical model (WirePosition) without tight coupling.

types.name: AsynchronousMachine
types.summary: A rotating machine whose shaft rotates asynchronously with the electrical field. Also known as an induction machine with no external connection to the rotor windings, e.g. squirrel-cage induction machine.

fields.name: asynchronousMachineType
fields.summary: Indicates the type of Asynchronous Machine (motor or generator).

fields.name: converterFedDrive
fields.summary: Indicates whether the machine is a converter fed drive. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: efficiency
fields.summary: Efficiency of the asynchronous machine at nominal operation as a percentage. Indicator for converter drive motors. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: iaIrRatio
fields.summary: Ratio of locked-rotor current to the rated current of the motor (Ia/Ir). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: nominalFrequency
fields.summary: Nameplate data indicates if the machine is 50 Hz or 60 Hz.

fields.name: nominalSpeed
fields.summary: Nameplate data. Depends on the slip and number of pole pairs.

fields.name: polePairNumber
fields.summary: Number of pole pairs of stator. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: ratedMechanicalPower
fields.summary: Rated mechanical power (Pr in IEC 60909-0). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: reversible
fields.summary: Indicates for converter drive motors if the power can be reversible. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: rr1
fields.summary: Damper 1 winding resistance.

fields.name: rr2
fields.summary: Damper 2 winding resistance.

fields.name: rxLockedRotorRatio
fields.summary: Locked rotor ratio (R/X). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: tpo
fields.summary: Transient rotor time constant (greater than tppo).

fields.name: tppo
fields.summary: Sub-transient rotor time constant (greater than 0).

fields.name: xlr1
fields.summary: Damper 1 winding leakage reactance.

fields.name: xlr2
fields.summary: Damper 2 winding leakage reactance.

fields.name: xm
fields.summary: Magnetizing reactance.

fields.name: xp
fields.summary: Transient reactance (unsaturated) (greater than or equal to xpp).

fields.name: xpp
fields.summary: Sub-transient reactance (unsaturated).

fields.name: xs
fields.summary: Synchronous reactance (greater than xp).

types.name: AsynchronousMachineKind
types.summary: Kind of Asynchronous Machine.

enumValues.name: generator
enumValues.summary: The Asynchronous Machine is a generator.

enumValues.name: motor
enumValues.summary: The Asynchronous Machine is a motor.

types.name: Breaker
types.summary: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal circuit conditions and also making, carrying for a specified time, and breaking currents under specified abnormal circuit conditions e.g. those of short circuit.

fields.name: inTransitTime
fields.summary: The transition time from open to close.

types.name: BusbarSection
types.summary: A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation. Voltage measurements are typically obtained from voltage transformers that are connected to busbar sections. A bus bar section may have many physical terminals but for analysis is modelled with exactly one logical terminal.

fields.name: VoltageControlZone
fields.summary: A VoltageControlZone is controlled by a designated BusbarSection.

fields.name: ipMax
fields.summary: Maximum allowable peak short-circuit current of busbar (Ipmax in IEC 60909-0). Mechanical limit of the busbar in the substation itself. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

types.name: Clamp
types.summary: A Clamp is a galvanic connection at a line segment where other equipment is connected. A Clamp does not cut the line segment. A Clamp is ConductingEquipment and has one Terminal with an associated ConnectivityNode. Any other ConductingEquipment can be connected to the Clamp ConnectivityNode.

fields.name: ClampAction
fields.summary: The clamp action that is performed on the clamp

fields.name: JumperAction
fields.summary: Action taken with this jumper.

fields.name: lengthFromTerminal1
fields.summary: The length to the place where the clamp is located starting from side one of the line segment, i.e. the line segment terminal with sequence number equal to 1.

types.name: CompositeSwitch
types.summary: A model of a set of individual Switches normally enclosed within the same cabinet and possibly with interlocks that restrict the combination of switch positions. These are typically found in medium voltage distribution networks. A CompositeSwitch could represent a Ring-Main-Unit (RMU), or pad-mounted switchgear, with primitive internal devices such as an internal bus-bar plus 3 or 4 internal switches each of which may individually be open or closed. A CompositeSwitch and a set of contained Switches can also be used to represent a multi-position switch e.g. a switch that can connect a circuit to Ground, Open or Busbar.

fields.name: Switches
fields.summary: Switches contained in this Composite switch.

fields.name: compositeSwitchType
fields.summary: An alphanumeric code that can be used as a reference to extra information such as the description of the interlocking scheme if any.

types.name: Conductor
types.summary: Combination of conducting material with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry current between points in the power system.

fields.name: length
fields.summary: Segment length for calculating line section capabilities.

types.name: Connector
types.summary: A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation and are modelled with a single logical terminal.

types.name: CoolantType
types.summary: Method of cooling a machine.

types.name: Cut
types.summary: A cut separates a line segment into two parts. The cut appears as a switch inserted between these two parts and connects them together. As the cut is normally open there is no galvanic connection between the two line segment parts. But it is possible to close the cut to get galvanic connection. The cut terminals are oriented towards the line segment terminals with the same sequence number. Hence the cut terminal with sequence number equal to 1 is oriented to the line segment's terminal with sequence number equal to 1. The cut terminals also act as connection points for jumpers and other equipment, e.g. a mobile generator. To enable this, connectivity nodes are placed at the cut terminals. Once the connectivity nodes are in place any conducting equipment can be connected at them.

fields.name: ACLineSegment
fields.summary: The line segment to which the cut is applied.

fields.name: lengthFromTerminal1
fields.summary: The length to the place where the cut is located starting from side one of the cut line segment, i.e. the line segment Terminal with sequenceNumber equal to 1.

types.name: DisconnectingCircuitBreaker
types.summary: A circuit breaking device including disconnecting function, eliminating the need for separate disconnectors.

types.name: Disconnector
types.summary: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for changing the connections in a circuit, or for isolating a circuit or equipment from a source of power. It is required to open or close circuits when negligible current is broken or made.

types.name: EarthFaultCompensator
types.summary: A conducting equipment used to represent a connection to ground which is typically used to compensate earth faults. An earth fault compensator device modelled with a single terminal implies a second terminal solidly connected to ground. If two terminals are modelled, the ground is not assumed and normal connection rules apply.

fields.name: r
fields.summary: Nominal resistance of device.

types.name: EnergyConnection
types.summary: A connection of energy generation or consumption on the power system model.

types.name: EnergyConsumer
types.summary: Generic user of energy - a point of consumption on the power system model. EnergyConsumer.pfixed, .qfixed, .pfixedPct and .qfixedPct have meaning only if there is no LoadResponseCharacteristic associated with EnergyConsumer or if LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is set to False.

fields.name: EnergyConsumerAction

fields.name: EnergyConsumerPhase

fields.summary: The load response characteristic of this load. If missing, this load is assumed to be constant power.

fields.name: grounded

fields.name: p
fields.summary: Active power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node. For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage. Starting value for a steady state solution.

fields.name: pfixed
fields.summary: Active power of the load that is a fixed quantity and does not vary as load group value varies. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

fields.name: pfixedPct
fields.summary: Fixed active power as a percentage of load group fixed active power. Used to represent the time-varying components. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

fields.name: phaseConnection
fields.summary: The type of phase connection, such as wye or delta.

fields.name: q
fields.summary: Reactive power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node. For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage. Starting value for a steady state solution.

fields.name: qfixed
fields.summary: Reactive power of the load that is a fixed quantity and does not vary as load group value varies. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

fields.name: qfixedPct
fields.summary: Fixed reactive power as a percentage of load group fixed reactive power. Used to represent the time-varying components. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

fields.name: pfixedPct

fields.name: q

fields.name: qfixed

fields.name: qfixedPct

types.name: EnergySource

fields.name: EnergySchedulingType

fields.name: pMin

fields.name: voltageMagnitude

types.name: ExternalNetworkInjection
types.summary: This class represents the external network and it is used for IEC 60909 calculations.

fields.name: governorSCD
fields.summary: Power Frequency Bias. This is the change in power injection divided by the change in frequency and negated. A positive value of the power frequency bias provides additional power injection upon a drop in frequency.

fields.name: ikSecond
fields.summary: Indicates whether initial symmetrical short-circuit current and power have been calculated according to IEC (Ik"). Used only if short circuit calculations are done according to superposition method.

fields.summary: Maximum initial symmetrical short-circuit currents (Ik" max) in A (Ik" = Sk"/(SQRT(3) Un)). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: maxP
fields.summary: Maximum active power of the injection.

fields.name: maxQ

fields.name: maxR0ToX0Ratio
fields.summary: Maximum ratio of zero sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its zero sequence reactance (R(0)/X(0) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: maxR1ToX1Ratio
fields.summary: Maximum ratio of positive sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its positive sequence reactance (R(1)/X(1) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: maxZ0ToZ1Ratio
fields.summary: Maximum ratio of zero sequence impedance to its positive sequence impedance (Z(0)/Z(1) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: minInitialSymShCCurrent
fields.summary: Minimum initial symmetrical short-circuit currents (Ik" min) in A (Ik" = Sk"/(SQRT(3) Un)). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: minP
fields.summary: Minimum active power of the injection.

fields.name: minQ
fields.summary: Minimum reactive power limit. It is used for modelling of infeed for load flow exchange and not for short circuit modelling.

fields.name: minR0ToX0Ratio

fields.name: minR1ToX1Ratio
fields.summary: Minimum ratio of positive sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its positive sequence reactance (R(1)/X(1) min). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

fields.name: minZ0ToZ1Ratio

types.name: PhaseTapChanger
types.summary: A transformer phase shifting tap model that controls the phase angle difference across the power transformer and potentially the active power flow through the power transformer. This phase tap model may also impact the voltage magnitude.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerAsymmetrical
types.summary: Describes the tap model for an asymmetrical phase shifting transformer in which the difference voltage vector adds to the in-phase winding. The out-of-phase winding is the transformer end where the tap changer is located. The angle between the in-phase and out-of-phase windings is named the winding connection angle. The phase shift depends on both the difference voltage magnitude and the winding connection angle.

fields.name: windingConnectionAngle
fields.summary: The phase angle between the in-phase winding and the out-of -phase winding used for creating phase shift. The out-of-phase winding produces what is known as the difference voltage. Setting this angle to 90 degrees is not the same as a symmetrical transformer. The attribute can only be multiples of 30 degrees. The allowed range is -150 degrees to 150 degrees excluding 0.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerLinear
types.summary: Describes a tap changer with a linear relation between the tap step and the phase angle difference across the transformer. This is a mathematical model that is an approximation of a real phase tap changer. The phase angle is computed as stepPhaseShiftIncrement times the tap position. The voltage magnitude of both sides is the same.

fields.name: stepPhaseShiftIncrement
fields.summary: Phase shift per step position. A positive value indicates a positive angle variation from the Terminal at the PowerTransformerEnd, where the TapChanger is located, into the transformer. The actual phase shift increment might be more accurately computed from the symmetrical or asymmetrical models or a tap step table lookup if those are available.

fields.name: xMax
fields.summary: The reactance depends on the tap position according to a "u" shaped curve. The maximum reactance (xMax) appears at the low and high tap positions. Depending on the �u� curve the attribute can be either higher or lower than PowerTransformerEnd.x.

fields.name: xMin
fields.summary: The reactance depends on the tap position according to a "u" shaped curve. The minimum reactance (xMin) appears at the mid tap position. PowerTransformerEnd. x shall be consistent with PhaseTapChangerLinear.xMin and PhaseTapChangerNonLinear.xMin. In case of inconsistency, PowerTransformerEnd.x shall be used.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerNonLinear
types.summary: The non-linear phase tap changer describes the non-linear behaviour of a phase tap changer. This is a base class for the symmetrical and asymmetrical phase tap changer models. The details of these models can be found in IEC 61970-301.

fields.name: voltageStepIncrement
fields.summary: The voltage step increment on the out of phase winding (the PowerTransformerEnd where the TapChanger is located) specified in percent of rated voltage of the PowerTransformerEnd. A positive value means a positive voltage variation from the Terminal at the PowerTransformerEnd, where the TapChanger is located, into the transformer. When the increment is negative, the voltage decreases when the tap step increases.

fields.name: xMax
fields.summary: The reactance depends on the tap position according to a "u" shaped curve. The maximum reactance (xMax) appears at the low and high tap positions. Depending on the �u� curve the attribute can be either higher or lower than PowerTransformerEnd.x.

fields.name: xMin
fields.summary: The reactance depend on the tap position according to a "u" shaped curve. The minimum reactance (xMin) appear at the mid tap position. PowerTransformerEnd. x shall be consistent with PhaseTapChangerLinear.xMin and PhaseTapChangerNonLinear.xMin. In case of inconsistency, PowerTransformerEnd.x shall be used.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerSymmetrical
types.summary: Describes a symmetrical phase shifting transformer tap model in which the voltage magnitude of both sides is the same. The difference voltage magnitude is the base in an equal-sided triangle where the sides corresponds to the primary and secondary voltages. The phase angle difference corresponds to the top angle and can be expressed as twice the arctangent of half the total difference voltage.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerTable
types.summary: Describes a tabular curve for how the phase angle difference and impedance varies with the tap step.

fields.name: PhaseTapChangerTabular
fields.summary: The phase tap changers to which this phase tap table applies.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerTablePoint
types.summary: Describes each tap step in the phase tap changer tabular curve.

fields.name: PhaseTapChangerTable
fields.summary: The table of this point.

fields.name: angle
fields.summary: The angle difference in degrees. A positive value indicates a positive angle variation from the Terminal at the PowerTransformerEnd, where the TapChanger is located, into the transformer.

types.name: PhaseTapChangerTabular
types.summary: Describes a tap changer with a table defining the relation between the tap step and the phase angle difference across the transformer.
